title: JevBench hosted-provider reference prices (shared with jevbench-gpu-round-20260919)
rule: A system with a public per-call or per-token tariff is priced at that tariff x measured tokens. A system without one (open weights, author demos, local CPU runs) is priced as if a large inference provider hosted it: the OpenRouter list price of the same weights; if OpenRouter does not list them, the nearest LARGER sibling on OpenRouter; if no sibling of the size class is on OpenRouter, the DeepInfra list price of the same weights or the nearest larger model of the same class. Never RunPod/per-minute GPU rental and never our own CPU time: providers buy capacity in bulk or own the GPUs. Price x tokens per decision (measured where the run reports usage, else the input tokens of the gemini-3.1-flash-lite run on the same prompts, which is how the other systems see the same state and rubric) = $ per 1,000 decisions, marked est.

encoder_classifier_<=0.6B.note: encoders are billed per input token only; nothing is generated

generative_<=1B.note: smallest generative model with an OpenRouter list price; DeepInfra is 5-20x cheaper, so this errs high

system-one-open.why: Gemma 4 E2B is not listed; the nearest larger sibling, Gemma 4 E4B, is listed only on DeepInfra

open-alternative-jev.why: same weights (not on OpenRouter); one forward pass, nothing generated

open-jev-deberta-v3-large.ref: deepinfra encoders of the same size (bge-large, e5-large, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B)
open-jev-deberta-v3-large.why: an encoder of the same size class; one forward pass, nothing generated

needle-3.why: no generative model under 1B is listed; the smallest listed one (1B) errs high; about 20 generated tokens for one tool call

qwen3.8-27b.why: same weights; our run used a flat-rate Chutes subscription
